    ...m literature reports.²¹,⁴⁰ The mass balance for titer, [B1], was applied only after 144 h, as earlier samples are typically below the concentration range for the assay. In addition, since the highest specific antibody production rate was observed in the G1 or G0-phase of the cell cycle based on literature reports,²,⁴,²¹ the fraction of arrested viable cells was introduced into the mass balance equation for [B1]. The fraction of viable cells ( $ X_V^{(d)} $) that are not undergoing propagation by the next sampling time ( $ t^{(d+1)} $) was estimated by the term $ (1 - \mu / \mu_{\text{max}}) $.
(6.1) \frac{d X_{V}}{d t} =(\mu-\mu_{d})\cdot X_{V}    [code: ODE, computes X_{V}, code proposes balance]
(6.2) \frac{d[\mathrm{GLC}]}{d t} =-\left((\mu-\mu_{d})/Y_{X_{V}/\mathrm{glc}}+m_{\mathrm{glc}}\right)\cdot X_{V}    [code: ODE, computes [GLC], code proposes balance]
(6.3) \frac{d[\mathrm{GLN}]}{d t} =-\left((\mu-\mu_{d})/Y_{X_{V}/\mathrm{g}\ln}+m_{\mathrm{g}\ln}\right)\cdot X_{V}-d_{g\ln}[\mathrm{GLN}]    [code: ODE, computes [GLN], code proposes balance]
(6.4) \frac{d[\mathrm{LAC}]}{d t} =Y_{\mathrm{lac}/\mathrm{glc}}\cdot\left((\mu-\mu_{d})/Y_{X_{V}/\mathrm{glc}}+m_{\mathrm{glc}}\right)\cdot X_{V}    [code: ODE, computes [LAC], code proposes balance]
(6.5) \frac{d[\mathrm{AMM}]}{d t} =Y_{\mathrm{amm}/\mathrm{g}\ln}\cdot\left((\mu-\mu_{d})/Y_{X_{V}/\mathrm{g}\ln}\right)\cdot X_{V}-r_{\mathrm{amm}}\cdot X_{V} +d_{\mathrm{g}\ln}[\mathrm{GLN}]    [code: ODE, computes [AMM], code proposes balance]
(6.6) \frac{d[\mathrm{B1}]}{d t} =Q_{B1}\cdot X_{V}\cdot\left(1-\frac{\mu}{\mu_{\max}}\right)\cdot[B1]    [code: ODE, computes [B1], code proposes balance]
    The values for $ \mu $ and $ \mu_d $, were calculated by Eq. 7. $ ^{1,2,41} $ As previously reported, $ ^{38} $ inhibition to cell growth became significant when ammonia and/or lactate reached concentrations of 5.1 and 58 mM, respectively (threshold values). Therefore, the ammonia or lactate was considered in Eq. 7 only when the concentration exceeded 90% of their threshold value, or 4.6 and 52 mM for ammonia and lactate, respectively.
(7.1) \mu=\mu_{\max} \frac{[GLC]}{K_{\mathrm{glc}}+[GLC]}\cdot\frac{[GLN]}{K_{\mathrm{g}\ln}+[GLN]}\cdot\frac{\mathrm{KI}_{\mathrm{lac}}}{KI_{\mathrm{lac}}+[LAC]} \cdot\frac{\mathrm{KI}_{\mathrm{amm}}}{KI_{\mathrm{amm}}+[AMM]}    [code: algebraic, computes \mu, code proposes constitutive]
(7.2) \mu_{d}=k_{d} \cdot\frac{[LAC]}{KD_{\mathrm{lac}}+[LAC]}\cdot\frac{[AMM]}{KD_{\mathrm{amm}}+[AMM]}    [code: algebraic, computes \mu_{d}, code proposes constitutive]
    where

Symbols:
  X_{V}: viable cell density [10^9 cells L^{-1}] (computed)
  \mu: specific cell growth rate [h^{-1}] (computed)
  \mu_{d}: specific cell death rate [h^{-1}] (computed)
  [GLC]: glucose concentration [mM] (computed)
  Y_{X_V/glc}: glucose yield coefficient [10^{11} cells mol^{-1}] (parameter)
  m_{glc}: glucose maintenance coefficient [10^{-12} mmol cell^{-1} h^{-1}] (parameter)
  [GLN]: glutamine concentration [mM] (computed)
  Y_{X_V/gln}: glutamine yield coefficient [10^{11} cells mol^{-1}] (parameter)
  m_{gln}: glutamine maintenance coefficient [10^{-12} mmol cell^{-1} h^{-1}] (computed)
  d_{gln}: first-order decomposition rate of glutamine [10^{-3} h^{-1}] (parameter)
  [LAC]: Lactate concentration [mM] (computed)
  Y_{lac/glc}: Lactate yield from glucose [mol mol^-1] (parameter)
  [AMM]: Ammonia concentration [mM] (computed)
  Y_{amm/gln}: Ammonia yield from glutamine [mol mol^-1] (parameter)
  r_{amm}: Ammonia removal rate [10^-12 mmol cell^-1 h^-1] (parameter)
  [B1]: B1 protein titer (computed)
  Q_{B1}: Specific B1 production rate [10^-12 L cell^-1 h^-1] (parameter)
  \mu_{\max}: Maximum specific cell growth rate [h^-1] (parameter)
  K_{glc}: Half-maximum-rate concentration of glucose for cell growth rate [mM] (parameter)
  K_{gln}: Half-maximum-rate concentration of glutamine for cell growth rate [mM] (parameter)
  KI_{lac}: Half-maximum-rate concentration of lactate for cell growth rate [mM] (parameter)
  KI_{amm}: Half-maximum-rate concentration of ammonia for cell growth rate [mM] (parameter)
  k_{d}: Maximum cell death rate [h^-1] (parameter)
  KD_{lac}: Half-maximum-rate concentration of lactate for cell death rate [mM] (parameter)
  KD_{amm}: Half-maximum-rate concentration of ammonia for cell death rate [mM] (parameter)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Specific growth rate is zero during the cell death phase.
  - Glucose and glutamine maintenance terms are zero when d ≤ 6.
  - Ammonia and lactate are considered in the growth-rate equation only above 90% of their thresholds.
  - The B1 mass balance is applied only after 144 h.

laws.description: Viable cell density changes through cell growth offset by cell death.
laws.law_type_reason: It expresses viable-cell accumulation as net growth minus death.

laws.description: Glucose concentration decreases through growth-associated and maintenance uptake by viable cells.
laws.law_type_reason: It gives glucose accumulation as consumption by viable cells.

laws.description: Glutamine concentration decreases through growth-associated uptake, maintenance uptake, and first-order decomposition.
laws.law_type_reason: It accounts for glutamine accumulation through cellular consumption and decomposition.

laws.description: Lactate concentration increases in proportion to glucose consumption, scaled by the lactate yield from glucose.
laws.law_type_reason: It gives lactate accumulation from its formation rate.

laws.description: Ammonia concentration changes through glutamine-related production and an ammonia removal term.
laws.law_type_reason: It accounts for ammonia accumulation from production and removal processes.

laws.description: B1 titer accumulation is computed from production by viable cells weighted by the estimated fraction of cells not propagating.
laws.quote: the fraction of arrested viable cells was introduced into the mass balance equation for [B1].
laws.law_type_reason: It expresses B1 titer accumulation through a production term.

laws.description: Specific cell growth rate is scaled by glucose and glutamine availability and reduced by lactate and ammonia inhibition.
laws.quote: inhibition to cell growth became significant when ammonia and/or lactate reached concentrations of 5.1 and 58 mM, respectively (threshold values). Therefore, the ammonia or lactate was considered in Eq. 7 only when the concentration exceeded 90% of their threshold value, or 4.6 and 52 mM for ammonia and lactate, respectively.
laws.law_type_reason: It defines growth rate using substrate saturation and inhibitor-dependent kinetic factors.

laws.description: Specific cell death rate increases with lactate and ammonia through saturating terms scaled by a maximum death rate.
laws.quote: The values for $ \mu $ and $ \mu_d $, were calculated by Eq. 7.
laws.law_type_reason: It defines the death-rate kinetics as a function of lactate and ammonia concentrations.
